Thessley security projects

Download packages only for the component you plan to use. Check the requirements and SHA-256 checksum before installing.

Installation guide targets: Ubuntu 24.04 LTS for Linux and Windows 11 for Windows.

Thessley Security Hardening for WordPress

Version 1.0.23 · ZIP package

Modular security features for WordPress. This project build is distributed for evaluation; install it on a staging site first and keep a site backup.

Download plugin ZIP SHA-256 checksums

Install the WordPress plugin

  1. Back up the site, then download the ZIP and verify its SHA-256 hash using the checksum file.
  2. In WordPress admin, open Plugins → Add Plugin → Upload Plugin.
  3. Select the ZIP, install it, and activate Thessley Security Hardening.
  4. Review the plugin dashboard and event log. Leave modules in log-only mode while confirming the events are correct.
  5. Test any enforcement setting on staging first. Keep a working administrator session and recovery path.

Windows SSH and web admin tools

Target OS: Windows 11. The standard package provides the Windows approval service, installer, HTTPS admin page, and setup guides. The desktop approval helper is a separate companion download. Both use the Thessley Passkey phone app.

Windows SSH + Web GUI

Windows OpenSSH QR approval service, HTTPS admin page, installer, and setup guides.

Download service package

Windows desktop approval helper

Desktop UI for enrolling a phone and approving supported Windows SSH requests. Requires the service package.

Download desktop helper
Experimental: Windows QR sign-in screen. This optional credential-provider prototype changes the Windows logon flow. Keep the normal PIN/password sign-in and a tested recovery method available; read the included rollback guide before installing.

Download experimental package Windows package SHA-256 checksums

Install the Windows SSH + Web GUI package

  1. Use Windows 11 and open PowerShell as Administrator. Install the Windows OpenSSH Server capability if it is missing, then start it at boot:
$cap = Get-WindowsCapability -Online -Name OpenSSH.Server~~~~0.0.1.0
if ($cap.State -ne 'Installed') {
  Add-WindowsCapability -Online -Name OpenSSH.Server~~~~0.0.1.0
}
Set-Service -Name sshd -StartupType Automatic
Start-Service sshd
Get-Service sshd

Windows normally creates the OpenSSH firewall rule during installation. Check it with Get-NetFirewallRule -Name OpenSSH-Server-In-TCP. If the rule is missing and SSH should be reachable only from the local network, create a Private-profile rule limited to the local subnet:

New-NetFirewallRule -Name 'OpenSSH-Server-In-TCP' -DisplayName 'OpenSSH Server (sshd)' `
  -Enabled True -Direction Inbound -Protocol TCP -Action Allow -LocalPort 22 `
  -Profile Private -RemoteAddress LocalSubnet

If you need SSH from a VPN, include the VPN subnet in the rule’s remote-address scope. Confirm a normal SSH connection works before adding Thessley’s account-specific SSH rules. See Microsoft’s OpenSSH Server installation guide.

  1. Install Python 3.10 or later for all users. For example, in administrator PowerShell:
winget install --id Python.Python.3.13 --scope machine
  1. Download and extract windows-ssh-webgui.zip, for example to C:ThessleyWindows-SSH-WebGUI.
  2. In administrator PowerShell, run the installer. Adjust the Python path if your installed version differs:
Set-Location C:ThessleyWindows-SSH-WebGUI
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .installinstall.ps1 `
  -Python "C:Program FilesPython313python.exe" `
  -OpenFirewall -OpenWebFirewall

The optional firewall switches allow the phone approval listener on TCP 47810 and the web page on TCP 47820 from the local subnet on Private networks. The installer does not edit sshd_config or restart OpenSSH.

  1. Run ThessleySignInTest.exe from the desktop approval helper, choose Enroll this account, and compare the pairing codes shown by the computer and phone before confirming.
  2. Turn on the web page and check its certificate fingerprint:
& "C:ProgramDataThessleyPamWinthessley-pam-win.cmd" web on
& "C:ProgramDataThessleyPamWinthessley-pam-win.cmd" web status

Open https://<Windows-computer-IP>:47820/ from the local network. Approve the sign-in on the phone and compare the browser certificate fingerprint with web status.

Enable QR approval for SSH

Keep an existing administrator SSH session open while changing the configuration. Back up C:ProgramDatasshsshd_config first. Generate the account-specific block, choosing the first factor you want:

& "C:ProgramDataThessleyPamWinthessley-pam-win.cmd" sshd-config --user YOURNAME --factor password
  • --factor password: Windows account password, then phone approval.
  • --factor key: SSH key, then phone approval.
  • --factor key-password: SSH key and account password, then phone approval.

Add the generated Match User block above the stock Match Group administrators block. Validate before restarting OpenSSH:

& "C:Program FilesOpenSSHsshd.exe" -t
Restart-Service sshd

Test from a second computer while keeping the original session open. If validation fails, do not restart the service.

Remove the Windows service

First remove the Thessley block from sshd_config, validate with sshd -t, and restart OpenSSH. Then run installuninstall.ps1 as administrator. The uninstaller refuses to remove the gate while OpenSSH still references it.

Android Passkey app

Version 0.1.11 · Android APK

Android companion app for Thessley phone approvals. Package: com.eagleeyeintelligence.thessleypasskey. Requires Android 8.0 or later.

Download Android APK SHA-256 checksums

Install the APK only if Android accepts its signature for your current installation. If Android reports a signature conflict, keep your installed copy and use the matching Play release when available. Do not uninstall an enrolled app to work around a signature conflict: uninstalling deletes its phone keys.

Linux computer tools

Linux source package · 22 October 2026

Documented target: Ubuntu 24.04 LTS on x86-64 or ARM64. The source package can also run on Debian or Armbian with systemd and the required dependencies, but the installation steps here are written for Ubuntu 24.04 LTS.

Download Linux source package SHA-256 checksums

The maintained Git repository is hosted in GitLab. It currently requires project access; this public source archive is available without a GitLab account.

Ubuntu 24.04 APT repository · 22 October 2026

For Ubuntu 24.04 on amd64 or ARM64, add the signed Thessley package repository hosted on the Orange Pi 5 and install the source-staging package:

sudo install -d -m 0755 /etc/apt/keyrings
curl -fsSL https://wp-opsec.eagleeye-intelligence.com/wp-content/uploads/thessley-apt/thessley-archive-keyring.gpg | sudo tee /etc/apt/keyrings/thessley-archive-keyring.gpg >/dev/null
sudo chmod 0644 /etc/apt/keyrings/thessley-archive-keyring.gpg
echo 'deb [arch=amd64,arm64 signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/thessley-archive-keyring.gpg] https://wp-opsec.eagleeye-intelligence.com/wp-content/uploads/thessley-apt stable main' | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/thessley.list
sudo apt update
sudo apt install thessley-pam-linux-installer

APT signing key fingerprint: 563A 4057 8A64 324A C1EB 0547 5B76 886E 9CDB 7C03. The package stages files under /opt/thessley-pam-linux and installs runtime dependencies. It does not enable services or change SSH, PAM, VPN, firewall, or desktop login policy. To install the shared approval service, run sudo /opt/thessley-pam-linux/install.sh explicitly. Removing the staging package with sudo apt remove thessley-pam-linux-installer does not undo separately installed components; use their documented uninstall steps. Keep the timed SSH configuration rollback armed when changing SSH or PAM.

Install the core service and web admin page

  1. Extract the archive and enter its directory. Install the system packages:
tar -xzf thessley-pam-linux-2026.10.22.tar.gz
cd thessley-pam-linux
sudo apt update
sudo apt install qrencode python3-cryptography python3-asn1crypto
  1. Install and check the shared phone approval service. This step does not change PAM or SSH login configuration:
sudo ./install.sh
sudo systemctl is-active thessley-pam-approvals.service
  1. Install the web admin service, enable it, and check its status:
sudo ./install-web.sh
sudo thessley-pam web on
sudo thessley-pam web status

The approval listener uses TCP 47810 and the web admin page uses TCP 47820. Allow those ports only from networks that should reach the computer, such as your trusted LAN or VPN. Enroll a phone in the web admin page before enabling any login integration.

OpenVPN with Thessley QR approval

This Ubuntu 24.04 setup requires both a per-device OpenVPN client certificate and a live approval on the enrolled phone for every connection. OpenVPN Connect 3.x can open the QR approval page automatically. Reconnects require a new phone approval; this setup does not issue reconnect tokens or a grace period.

If you already run OpenVPN, back up its configuration and merge the Thessley authentication directives into it; do not replace a working server configuration wholesale. The commands below describe a new server named thessley.

  1. Install OpenVPN, Easy-RSA, and the Thessley VPN approval service. The Thessley core service must already be installed:
sudo apt update
sudo apt install openvpn easy-rsa
sudo /opt/thessley-pam-linux/install-vpn.sh
  1. Create an OpenVPN certificate authority and server certificate. Protect the CA private key and keep an offline backup:
sudo make-cadir /etc/openvpn/easy-rsa-thessley
sudo -i
cd /etc/openvpn/easy-rsa-thessley
./easyrsa init-pki
EASYRSA_ALGO=ec EASYRSA_CURVE=prime256v1 ./easyrsa build-ca
EASYRSA_BATCH=1 EASYRSA_ALGO=ec EASYRSA_CURVE=prime256v1 ./easyrsa build-server-full server nopass
openvpn --genkey secret pki/ta.key
install -d -m 0755 /etc/openvpn/server
install -o root -g root -m 0644 pki/ca.crt /etc/openvpn/server/ca.crt
install -o root -g root -m 0644 pki/issued/server.crt /etc/openvpn/server/server.crt
install -o root -g root -m 0600 pki/private/server.key /etc/openvpn/server/server.key
install -o root -g root -m 0600 pki/ta.key /etc/openvpn/server/ta.key
exit
  1. Create /etc/openvpn/server/thessley.conf for a new VPN server. Choose a tunnel range that does not overlap your LAN or other VPNs:
sudo tee /etc/openvpn/server/thessley.conf >/dev/null <<'EOF'
port 1194
proto udp
dev tun
topology subnet
server 10.8.0.0 255.255.255.0
ca ca.crt
cert server.crt
key server.key
dh none
tls-crypt ta.key
tls-version-min 1.2
remote-cert-tls client
verify-client-cert require
script-security 2
auth-user-pass-verify /usr/local/lib/thessley-pam/vpn-auth via-env
reneg-sec 0
push "reneg-sec 0"
user nobody
group nogroup
keepalive 10 120
persist-key
persist-tun
verb 3
EOF
  1. Set the public DNS name (or stable public IP) phones will use, then enroll the VPN phone while it is on the server’s network. Replace ubuntu with the Linux account that will own this VPN login:
sudo thessley-pam vpn public-host vpn.example.org
sudo thessley-pam vpn enroll ubuntu
sudo thessley-pam vpn on
sudo systemctl enable --now openvpn-server@thessley
sudo thessley-pam vpn status
sudo systemctl status --no-pager openvpn-server@thessley

Point vpn.example.org at your public IP. Forward UDP 1194 and TCP 47830 on the router to this computer. TCP 47830 serves the expiring QR approval page and phone response; UDP 1194 carries the VPN. If UFW is active, allow those two ports there as well. Avoid exposing the unrelated SSH and web-admin ports to the internet.

  1. Create a separate client profile for every device. Replace the account and device names. The generated .ovpn file contains that device’s private key; transfer it over a trusted channel and remove the extra copy afterward:
sudo /opt/thessley-pam-linux/vpn-new-client.sh ubuntu phone

Import ubuntu-phone.ovpn into OpenVPN Connect or another compatible client. At sign-in, use ubuntu as the username (the password field is ignored), then approve the QR/link on the enrolled phone. OpenVPN Connect 3.x opens the QR page; other clients may require opening the pending-authentication URL from their log. Review the full docs/VPN.md guide in the Linux source archive before adapting routes or NAT for access to the rest of your LAN. The setup follows Ubuntu’s OpenVPN guide and OpenVPN’s Easy-RSA quickstart.

Optional SSH integration with automatic rollback

The SSH module install does not edit SSH or PAM policy. Keep your current SSH session open, arm rollback before editing either login configuration file, and make sure you can reach the computer locally or through another recovery path.

sudo ./install-ssh.sh
sudo ./ssh-config-rollback.sh arm 10

After making the SSH/PAM changes described in docs/SSH.md, validate and reload:

sudo sshd -t && sudo systemctl reload ssh

Open a new terminal and verify a fresh SSH login. To finalize and keep the changes, run this from the verified session before the timer expires:

sudo ./ssh-config-rollback.sh cancel

If the test login fails or the timer expires, the saved SSH and PAM files are restored automatically and SSH is reloaded. Keep the original session open until the new session is verified. For other components, use their matching uninstall-*.sh script to roll back installation; read the component guide before enabling its login integration.

Verify package checksums · Linux GitLab repository (project access required) · Android GitLab repository (project access required)
